{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZZXQ0g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDArt8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 47, "title": "Implement 8253 binary mode-3 count/OUT sequencing and rising-edge IRQ0", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `e382535d3d11d2e137d9e0feeda226b66f9ef468`, mode 3 still uses the generic countdown in [Counter::tick](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e382535d3d11d2e137d9e0feeda226b66f9ef468/src/devices.rs#L224). It decrements once per clock, toggles OUT once per full divisor, and reports expiration without distinguishing falling from rising edges. Large batches also toggle only once regardless of elapsed periods.

This affects ordinary boot behavior: [the synthetic firmware](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e382535d3d11d2e137d9e0feeda226b66f9ef468/guest/firmware.asm#L33) programs mode 3. The [beeper mixer](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e382535d3d11d2e137d9e0feeda226b66f9ef468/src/bus.rs#L326) derives its level from the raw count, so correcting the counter requires a corresponding adjustment to its mode-3 consumer.

## Expected outcome

Implement binary mode-3 count/OUT sequencing on all three counters, with GATE held high, through both existing timer port banks on VM and Ap.

Hardware contract:

- Encodings `011` and `111` select mode 3. Support divisors 2–65,536; encoded zero represents 65,536.
- Mode programming sets OUT high and awaits a complete initial count. The next PIT clock loads it without also decrementing.
- Even counts decrement by two, reload the full divisor at terminal count and toggle OUT. Odd counts first decrement by one during the high half and by three during the low half; subsequent decrements are two. High/low durations are therefore `ceil(N/2)` and `floor(N/2)` clocks.
- Ordinary reads and count latches expose this sequence without stopping counting. Do not assert undefined pre-load count values.

Use the original [Intel 8253/8253-5 datasheet, Control Word Format, Counter Loading, Mode 3 and Read/Write Procedures](https://web.cecs.pdx.edu/~mpj/llp/references/8253.pdf). Anchor traces, starting at the initial load clock, are:

| Divisor | Successive `(count, OUT)` samples |
| --- | --- |
| 4 | `(4,H), (2,H), (4,L), (2,L), (4,H)` |
| 5 | `(5,H), (4,H), (2,H), (5,L), (2,L), (5,H)` |

Feed actual OUT0 rising transitions into the existing PIC latch, including programming-induced rises. Falling transitions and held-high output must not generate requests. Preserve the existing coalescing of elapsed requests. This follows [Intel’s 8259A IR-input and edge-triggered-mode specifications](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=17).

Derive mode-3 beeper samples from OUT while retaining the existing enable, amplitude, sampling and bounded-queue contracts.

Scope is initial programming, steady counting, ordinary read/latch visibility, OUT consumers, reprogramming through a new mode word and reset. Active divisor rewrites without a new mode word, external GATE behavior, BCD, divisor 1, other PIT modes and audio resampling improvements are non-goals and must remain explicitly outstanding.

## Context and reproduction

Static reproduction, not executed by this evaluator:

```rust
let mut pit = pc98_rust::devices::Pit::default();
pit.write(3, 0x36);
pit.write(0, 4);
pit.write(0, 0);
pit.tick(5); // One PIT clock under the existing conversion.
assert_eq!((pit.c[0].remaining, pit.c[0].output), (4, true));
```

Source inspection predicts baseline `(3, false)`. Existing [PIT tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e382535d3d11d2e137d9e0feeda226b66f9ef468/tests/pit.rs) provide clock conversion, batching and integration patterns, but their detailed traces target mode 2.

Project progress: the Coordinator reports PR #46’s bounded mode-2 implementation, baseline negative controls, 172 native integration passes and 66 production-Wasm browser passes. [The validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e382535d3d11d2e137d9e0feeda226b66f9ef468/docs/validation.md#issue-45-8253-binary-mode-2-2026-10-23) documents alternate browser ports with assertions and budgets preserved. This evaluator inspected source, relevant diffs and reports only. Remote CI success and independent PR review are unestablished. Supplied open Issues are empty; the recent mode-2 improvement does not implement this behavior.

All 26 inventory categories retain their fixed scopes and statuses:

| Status | Categories |
| --- | --- |
| partial | cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, bios, lio, integration |
| unimplemented | paging, fpu, rtc |
| implemented_unverified | ide, grcg, pcm86 |

PIT remains partial after this Issue. Remaining work includes active mode-3 rewrites, mode-0 continuation after terminal count, mode-specific behavior for 1/4/5, GATE/retriggering, BCD, divisor-1 behavior, comprehensive latch/access sequencing and fuller beeper timing. Protected execution, paging and basic FPU remain required project goals. Limited probes and six-game reports do not establish full accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add the minimal reproduction above and demonstrate its failure on the stated baseline and success after implementation. Record commands and actual outcomes.
- [ ] Add independent specification-derived Rust count/OUT/edge traces for divisors 2, 3, 4 and 5, plus boundary checks for 65,535 and encoded zero. Cover both mode encodings, all three counters and LSB-only, MSB-only and paired loading. Test incomplete initial writes, the separate load clock and ordinary latched reads while counting continues.
- [ ] Compare single-clock advancement with irregular batches and batches spanning many half-periods, including `u32::MAX` scheduler cycles. Require identical final counter/OUT/fractional state and aggregate rising-edge results, including batches whose endpoints hide intervening transitions. Advance large batches with bounded arithmetic.
- [ ] Exercise both profiles and port banks, channel isolation, programming-induced rises, absence of falling-edge requests, PIC masks/IRR/ISR/EOI, IF-clear/HLT delivery followed by IRET, transitions between modes 2 and 3, and reset during active/partial programming. Preserve the current scheduler-to-PIT conversion.
- [ ] Adapt only the mode-3 beeper consumer as necessary. Retain the existing square-wave frequency, silence, enable and queue-bound regressions. Correct the obsolete mode-3 latch expectation in `tests/core.rs::pit_keyboard_and_beeper` using documented traces, account for setup IRQ edges separately, and preserve its keyboard/beeper assertions.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built boot probe with offline preparation and a checked manifest recording source/image hashes, assembly command, provenance, exact guest-owned results/guards and a fixed execution budget. It must distinguish the baseline countdown through latched-count checks and exercise periodic hardware IRQ0 with EOI/IRET. Hosts may boot, step and inspect; they must not inject IRQs or manufacture results.
- [ ] Run the identical probe natively and through production-release Wasm on VM and Ap, before/after reset, at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/` browser roots. Require exact results/guards, PASS without FAIL, unchanged disk bytes and no host/browser errors within the declared budget, capped at 2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot.
- [ ] The Coordinator prepares legal source-backed fixtures and runs the [repository reproduction checks](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e382535d3d11d2e137d9e0feeda226b66f9ef468/README.md#reproduce-the-checks), including `cargo test --locked --test pit`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `npm test`. Preserve existing mode-2, PIC/SMM, BIOS timer, CPU-shadow, DOS/application, VM and game assertions and budgets. Report failures, skips and any equivalent port-only browser configuration honestly.
- [ ] Update focused hardware/provenance/validation documentation and existing CI fixture preparation. Preserve every inventory category and scope; retain PIT’s partial status and explicit remaining limitations. Run `git diff --check`. Use original Rust implementation and original/licensed tests; acquire no commercial ROMs or guest software.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
